clue.text: Come April, losing head could be a trickster

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters may be reshaped into something else
losing head means the word April drops its first letter

explanation.surface: Come the first of April, someone who has lost their head could play a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' cuts April to PRIL; with COME that gives COMEPRIL, which 'could be' rearranges. The April-fool picture hides the crossword setter, who is the real trickster.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword setter sets out to mislead solvers, so playfully calling one a trickster is fair.

clue.text: Wine — and where you might get it on account

parts.note: wine is sold in bars, the places you might get it

explanation.surface: A wine, and a note of where you might buy it on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the wine, so the bars are where you get it, and 'on' simply puts AC next to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white wine from Bordeaux in France, named after its village.

clue.text: "Night" steward

parts.note: read Night as short for Shakespeare's comedy Twelfth Night: the clue asks for the steward of Olivia's household in that play

explanation.definitionFit: Malvolio is the pompous steward to Olivia in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.

clue.text: The songbird diverted hikers

indicators.note: hikers sent off their route are diverted, so their letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Walkers are sent off course on a bird-watching trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrike, or butcher-bird, is a perching bird of the songbird order.

clue.text: Lady in centre of lake in waterproof clothing

indicators.note: in places the lady inside the letters taken from the lake
centre of picks the two middle letters of the word lake

parts.note: Nora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman stands in the middle of a lake wearing a rain jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is the container signal; the second is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak is a hooded waterproof jacket, an item of rainwear.

clue.text: What'll we hear?

parts.note: say the first word out loud and it sounds like the Australian name for this tree, so the clue is a sound-alike definition

explanation.walkthrough: 'What'll' spoken sounds like 'wattle', the Australian name for these trees: the clue defines the answer by its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian wattles belong to the genus Acacia, so a wattle tree is an acacia.

clue.text: City, very large, giving a sense of anticlimax

parts.note: Bath is an English city in Somerset
OS is short for outsize, very large in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A big city disappoints the visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) marks extra-large clothing in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is a ludicrous drop from the elevated to the trivial, which leaves an anticlimactic effect.

clue.text: Do up at Stationery Office is a source of pleasure

parts.note: SO is the abbreviation for the Stationery Office, the UK government publisher
to lace a shoe is to do it up

explanation.surface: Tidying up at the government printers turns out to be a pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' puts LACE beside SO; the Stationery Office is the British government's official publisher.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is comfort in distress, something that gives relief and pleasure.

clue.text: 1 supporting style is one to show the way

indicators.note: in a down entry a piece supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: a trend is a fashion or style
the answer to 1 Down is the compiler, which is another word for a crossword setter

explanation.surface: A trickster backing a fashion becomes its pioneer.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' points to 1 Down, COMPILER, whose synonym SETTER goes under TREND because 'supporting' in a down light means below.
explanation.definitionFit: A trendsetter leads fashion, one whose example others follow, showing them the way.

clue.text: Theatrical American university buildings

parts.note: camp means affectedly theatrical and exaggerated
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: Showy American college architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds and buildings of a university or college.

clue.text: Army unit to cover half a mile making a call

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to veil something is to cover it

indicators.note: half a picks the second half of the four-letter word mile

explanation.surface: Soldiers cover half a mile on a march to a bugle call.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle call that wakes soldiers in the morning.

clue.text: River I shall cut short to get a small one

parts.note: I'll is the shortened form of I shall

explanation.surface: A river is reduced to a mere stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a small one' stands for a small river, picking up 'River' from the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A rill is a tiny brook, a little stream of water.

clue.text: Study effect of power when not in the Union

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: when not tells us the following word in is missing from the word before it

parts.note: influence is the effect that power has over others

explanation.surface: Consider what power achieves once outside the Union.
explanation.walkthrough: INFLUENCE without its IN is FLUENCE; 'the Union' looks political but is a joining of rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A confluence is the place where two rivers meet and join, a union of streams.

clue.text: Argue with solver initially taken in by puzzles?

indicators.note: taken in by puts the letter inside the following word

parts.note: crosswords are word puzzles

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of solver

explanation.surface: Puzzles seem to quarrel with whoever is solving them.
explanation.walkthrough: The S from 'solver initially' goes into CROSSWORDS after CROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross swords with someone is an idiom for having an argument with them.

clue.text: Girl musicians providing dance music

parts.note: Sara is a girl's name
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A girl and her group play music for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A saraband is a slow stately Spanish dance, and the music written for it.

clue.text: Understand movement presented by the conductor

definitions.text: Understand movement presented by the conductor

parts.words: Understand movement presented by the conductor
parts.note: split the first word as under-stand to hint at a downward stroke: the clue describes the gesture a conductor makes to mark the first beat of a bar

explanation.definitionFit: The downbeat is the conductor's downward stroke of the baton, marking the first beat of the bar.

clue.text: Fast food, tho', if badly cooked could be a worry

indicators.note: if badly cooked suggests mangling the short word before it

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
to dog someone is to worry or pester them

explanation.surface: Junk food that has been badly prepared could be cause for concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if badly cooked' turns THO into HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot dog, a sausage in a bun, is classic fast food.

clue.text: Agree to remove top player, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the phrase is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to remove is to axe, and the top player in a tennis draw is the number one seed, giving axe seed

explanation.surface: A committee agrees to drop its best performer.
explanation.walkthrough: AXE SEED spoken sounds like the answer; seeds are ranked players in a tennis draw.
explanation.definitionFit: To accede to a request is to agree to it or consent.

clue.text: One writing publicity stuff to indulge in plagiarism?

definitions.meaning: someone who writes the text of advertisements
playfully, one who copies a writer's work

explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; the question mark flags the jokey second reading, someone who copies another writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A copywriter writes advertising copy, and the split reading suggests a plagiarist who copies writers.

clue.text: Delivery man turning up at roadside endlessly

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Roy is a man's name

indicators.note: endlessly means the word kerb loses its last letter

parts.note: the kerb is the edge of the pavement at the roadside

explanation.surface: A delivery driver appears at the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: ROY read upwards gives YOR; KERB without its end is KER. A YORKER is a cricket ball pitched right at the batter's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a yorker is a ball delivered to land at the batter's toes, one kind of delivery.

clue.text: Split involving Church not long ago

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase defining an adjective, as in 'of not long ago'

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A schism in the church happened lately.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recent happened a short time ago, lately rather than long past.

clue.text: Northern town's lighter part

definitions.meaning: a town in Caithness in the far north of Scotland
the part of a candle or oil lamp that is lit

explanation.definitionFit: Wick is a town in the north of Scotland, and a wick is the burning strand of a candle.

clue.text: Winning oar blade at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An oar blade out on the water looks like a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning in the sense of charming or endearing, as in a winning smile.

clue.text: Aussie pal's personal stuff left out

indicators.note: out tells us the letter for left is dropped

parts.note: cobblers, from rhyming slang cobbler's awls, is British slang for testicles, a man's personal equipment

explanation.surface: A mate from Australia leaves his belongings behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's works both ways: 'Aussie pal's' and 'cobbler's' (rhyming slang, cobbler's awls) share it, so L leaves COBBLER to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobber is Australian and New Zealand slang for a friend or mate.

clue.text: Name target mainly set in place for hitchers

indicators.note: set means arranged, so these letters are put in a new order
mainly means most of target, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A name is placed on a target somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: N with TARGE makes NTARGE for 'set' to rearrange. Gretna Green, just over the Scottish border, is famous for runaway weddings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gretna Green in Scotland is the traditional place where eloping couples got married, or hitched.

clue.text: New year pupils in remove

parts.note: to take something is to remove it

explanation.surface: This year's new pupils are in the remove form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remove' looks like the old name for a school form, which fits the surface, but it means take away.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's intake is the group of pupils admitted at the start of a year.
